review: Independent re-derivation of attempt a2's refutation (a2 is from another machine) using machinery that shares no code with it: a layered dynamic program over levels in exact integers, no probes/lib and no scipy, respecting the level restriction the task's referee warns about. From a2's ten marks alone: the one-set is the same in [0,3]^3 and [-2,6]^3 (37 sites, 1 seed, 9 amplified, 27 processed, level sizes 1,3,3,4,3,6,7,6,3,1); 333 is processed with all three 1-predecessors processed; v(233)=v(323)=v(332)=0 (tight) and v(333)=+1, so (Q), block 33's tight-sibling lemma and the rooted inequality (H) all fail; min(E-|A|)=1 and min(E-(10/9)|A|)=0 at that root, so c*(eta,333)=10/9 exactly, with and without the level restriction. New: the witness is mark-minimal - dropping any one of the nine non-seed marks stops 333 being processed-type. A node-closure integer program agrees with the DP at all four sites. This verifies a refutation rather than proving something new about the lemma's scope.
what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 1 of 4: Is the tight-sibling lemma's hypothesis ever satisfied?. GIVEN (refereed censuses): on every small window examined (2x2x2, 3x2x2, the isolated depth-2 cone, the named witnesses) a processed site never has ALL its 1-predecessors tight; the lemma's conclusion was therefore never tested. CAUTION from the referee: probes/lib/family.py's brute_min omits the definition's level restriction (nodes at levels <= level(z)); use probes/lib/rooted.py or restrict it yourself, and for windows with several seeds the single-seed dynamic program gives only upper bounds. TASK: prove or refute: a processed site with at least two processed 1-predecessors cannot have all of them tight (rooted value 0). If true the open lemma of block 33 (PR #8177) is vacuous-true and the unit budget c* = 1 follows (threshold 453 by that route; note the refinement-history route already gives 84). Route: a tight processed site forces a specific local pattern of marks below it (characterize all tight sites at depth <= 3 exhaustively with the correct definition), and two such patterns cannot share the cone of a common successor. ROUND 2: the first round's attempts and referee reports are under probes/work/derive/<problem>/ and logs/probes/J:derive:*/ and logs/probes/J:confirm:J-derive-*/ (python3 probes/harvest.py lists them); what survived refereeing is stated below as GIVEN, what failed is stated as the gap. DELIVERABLE, in your unit worktree on ai/probes: probes/work/derive/tight-sibling-vacuity/<your worker name>/ATTEMPT.md and check.py. ATTEMPT.md: (1) the exact statement you attempt; (2) numbered steps, each marked PROVED (argument given in full), CHECKED (a finite fact check.py verifies exactly) or ASSUMED; (3) if the route fails, the FIRST step that fails and why: a precise no-go for a route is a result; (4) what would finish it. check.py: exact arithmetic (fractions, integers, sympy) for every finite claim; it prints `SUMMARY: PROVED ...`, `SUMMARY: COUNTEREXAMPLE ...`, `SUMMARY: PARTIAL <what is new and exact>` or `SUMMARY: ROUTE FAILS AT <step>`, and a line `HIT: <the claim>` ONLY when you claim a proof, a counterexample, or a new exact partial result others can build on; a HIT is handed to a worker of another model family to referee line by line, so write for a hostile reader. Rules: definitions come from the notes on the PR branches named above (git fetch origin <branch>; git show origin/<branch>:<note>; find them with gh pr view <n> --json files,headRefName); any outside theorem you use must be re-proved at the scope you use it or listed under ASSUMED; no status words (proved theorems are promoted by the supervisor after the referee). Have your own plan BEFORE reading the prior attempts printed at claim time; then either build on a refereed partial result or take a different route. Run: python3 probes/run_probe.py <task> --worker <name> --model <model> --review "..." --extra "python3 probes/work/derive/tight-sibling-vacuity/<name>/check.py"

triage.note: The run demonstrates what it claims and is honest about being a verification rather than a discovery. 11 assertions, all exact: the realization is rebuilt from the ten marks in two boxes and agrees, the kinds and level sizes are counted, and the rooted values come from a layered dynamic program over levels in exact integers whose state is the subset of one-sites at a level - exact because every predecessor of a level l+1 site lies at level l, and the widest level holds 7 sites. It uses no probes/lib and no scipy, so it shares no code with attempt a2 whose refutation it reproduces, and it respects the level restriction that the task's referee warns brute_min omits. Confirmed: v(233)=v(323)=v(332)=0 with all three processed-type, v(333)=+1, so (Q), block 33's tight-sibling lemma and the rooted inequality (H) fail at this realization; and min(E-c|A|) = 1, 0, -1/100, -1 at c = 1, 10/9, 1001/900, 11/9 in exact rationals, so c*(eta,333) = 10/9 with and without the level restriction. New relative to a2: the witness is mark-minimal, since dropping any one of the nine non-seed marks stops 333 being processed-type. An optional node-closure integer program agrees with the DP at all four sites, by a different encoding from the library's flow formulation. NOT claimed, and section 3 says so: this proves nothing new about the lemma's scope, minimality is tested only for single-mark removal at this root so a smaller witness elsewhere is not excluded, and a2's inference about block 33's threshold is taken as read.
